M1's issue facet: a(kind) #MMA + every other warp instruction 1 <= T SMSP-cycles, a the least (T - #other)/#MMA over every gated program that holds the kind's MMA (beside IADD3+FFMA, which issues 0.973 a SMSP-cycle alone, beside IADD3 and the other lanes, duo, alone); every coefficient x 0.98 (2% noise) / 1.0094 (decision 76: the most the search's latest extension, r20261017-093959-b94b r20261017-094802-070d, moved a kind's least)

A-DISPATCH: a SMSP's scheduler issues at most 1 warp instruction a SMSP-cycle, of any kind, uniform included (the SM's 4 partitions each with one warp scheduler and one dispatch unit: Volta-onward architecture whitepapers)

A-TENSOR: the tensor cores do at most the data sheet's dense peak a SM-clock for the form's type, a 2:4 sparse form twice that on its logical k; a form's SMSP-cycles are its MACs over a quarter of it. A100 (whitepaper and data sheet at 1410 MHz, 108 SMs): dense MACs a SM-clock s8 2048, s4 4096, f16/bf16 1024, tf32 512, f64 64, b1 16384

A-PIPE: the alu pipe (Nsight Compute: logic, bit manipulation, integer except IMAD/IMUL) at 64 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.0: 32-bit add, compare/min/max, bitwise, shift), 2 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction

A-PIPE: the fma pipe (Nsight Compute: FP32, IMAD/IMUL and integer dot products) at 64 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.0: FP32 add/multiply/multiply-add 64, 32-bit integer multiply-add 64), 2 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction

A-PIPE: XU (transcendentals and conversions) at 16 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.0: 32-bit reciprocal, rsqrt, log2, exp2, sin, cos), 8 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction
A-PIPE: SHFL at 32 results a SM-clock (CUDA C++ Programming Guide 12.9 'Arithmetic Instructions' throughput table, CC 8.0: warp shuffle), 4 SMSP-cycles a warp instruction

A-SMEM: shared memory serves a request's distinct banks together, at most 128 B a SM-clock (Programming Guide 'Shared Memory': 32 banks, each 32 bits a clock), reads and writes alike; a broadcast load or a store to one address moves as little as one word, so each LDS/LDSM/STS warp instruction holds one request, 4 SMSP-cycles, whatever its width
